key_insight: Using the entrywise maximum matrix norm yields an exact mixed-integer quadratic reformulation of Wasserstein distributionally robust, chance-constrained quadratic optimization over the simplex.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports risk-aware allocation problems, including portfolio optimization and machine learning, when quadratic costs are estimated from sampled uncertain matrices.
method: Model distributional uncertainty with a Wasserstein ball around the sampled distribution.
Exploit linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to derive an exact mixed-integer quadratic formulation under the entrywise maximum norm.
Interpret the objective as worst-case Value-at-Risk and identify settings that reduce to a single deterministic instance.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on positive-definite and indefinite instances assess how model parameters affect optimal values and solution times, highlighting the computational cost of indefiniteness.
watch_item: Exact reformulation does not eliminate nonconvexity: indefinite quadratic instances can remain computationally expensive.
paper_title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
